**Verdict: ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Effort: max (issue label `effort:max`), no escalation.

## What looks good

- The layer mode is opt-in, and no caller turns it on. `PlayWorker::spawn_layered` has no caller outside the tests, so the product picture does not change. `camcraft-app` gets no `camcraft-gpu` edge, and the worker builds no second `wgpu` instance.
- Each move has one owner. A plain op (no rotary, turning, undercut or drill) whose tool is a ball or a flat end mill, with linear upright moves, goes to the layer. Every other op stays on the f64 field. `FieldPlay::cut` skips exactly the ops that the layer holds (`crates/app/src/stock_play_cut.rs:140`). The field never cuts a layer op, and every move is cut by exactly one owner.
- The layer at move k is the max-law fold of the layer ops' moves before k (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/layer_play.rs:13`). A keyframe at or before k plus the moves after it gives the value at k, in any batching and after a backward seek. The seek test proves this bit for bit against an independent one-batch fold at forward, jump, backward and end seeks.
- A layer fault turns the mode off and rebuilds the field from the uncut stock with every op (`stock_play_cut.rs:117`). The rebuilt field is bit-equal to the plain field picture.
- Prime Directive: this is display only. The verdict (`simulate_document`) and the post gate still run on the f64 truth. No verdict reads the layer (`layer_play.rs:6`). A shown layer can never pass an unsafe program.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` is added outside tests. The math is checked or saturating. The initial layer and the work items use `try_reserve_exact` and return a named `Err` on a failed allocation (`layer_play.rs:130`). Degenerate input is refused by name.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2629-gpu-playback-layer.md` is complete. Every new module has a provenance line. The PR touches no process file, no `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, and no snapshot PNG.

## Results (trial merge with main `aedd9750c`: clean; built locally)

- Build: `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-app --no-run`: ok.
- `camcraft-sim` lib: 241 passed. `stock_cut_twin`: 12 passed (the four layer tests and `the_gpu_kernel_fixtures_match_the_twin`). `stock_sim`: 24 passed.
- `camcraft-gpu` lib: 9 passed. `cut_onto`: 6 passed - the GPU parity ran on llvmpipe (Vulkan), `max |GPU - CPU law| 0e0`, and the device-loss test ran. `cut_parity`: 9 passed.
- `camcraft-app` lib: 306 passed. `stock_play_picture`: 5 passed (the three new layer tests). `stock_play`: 8. `stock_play_partial`: 4. `stock_play_precalc`: 9 (1 ignored). `stock_play_stop`: 3. `stock_view`: 4. `stock_sim_document`: 9.
- Clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The combined `cargo xtask gate quick` hit my 10-minute command cap during its app build and gave no verdict. I built the three crates and ran the touched binaries directly instead.

## Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath changed, so the example catalog suites do not apply.
- Light lane: `cargo xtask gate light` - 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (11 light twins), 6.6 min.
- This is a P2 PR, so it gets no heavy step (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes

- CPU and GPU layer laws. `the_gpu_kernel_fixtures_match_the_twin` proves the GPU kernel equals the one-batch CPU twin bit for bit. It does not exercise the layer's incremental `run_twin_items_onto`. The incremental law is proved against the one-batch fold by `the_layer_playback_is_the_one_batch_twin_at_every_seek` (through `cpu_layer_cutter`). The GPU onto-keyframe path (`cut_onto_or_cpu_on`, the cutter of S3c) is proved against the CPU onto law by `cut_onto`, at margin 0e0 on llvmpipe. The composition of a GPU cutter inside `LayerPlay` is not wired in this slice; S3c does it.
- The 256 MiB budget (`layer_play.rs:50`) bounds keyframe retention, not the working layer. At the packed lattice's `MAX_TEXELS` (1<<23 texels, 32 MiB for one layer) it holds about 8 keyframes. Past the budget, keyframes are thinned, and the value at k stays exact. The working allocation is bounded by `MAX_TEXELS` upstream and cleared with a named `Err`. No bug; I note the bound for clarity.
- The budget-thinning path and the worker-level fault frame are not exercised end to end. The test lattice is small, and the fault is tested on `FieldPlay`. Both are display only and use tested machinery.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` is 409 lines. It shrank from 430 in this PR, so the 400-line law does not flag it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
